note: Retirement gates for duplicate FX code and Zig responsibilities. A gate is met only when check_retirement.py proves it. Blocked entries must name their blockers.

retired.what: fx-core and fx-provider-http crates in rkendel1/chip-rs
retired.gate: chip-rs has no crate named fx-core, fx-provider-http or fx-single-attempt

blockers: HttpProviderConfig / config_from_env still live in chip-legacy-http and must move to chip-cli or chip-inference
Ollama's own API is served only by the legacy executor (decide: build it natively or drop it)
tests and mocks still construct the legacy provider (see legacy-http-consumers.txt)
one OpenRouter live run with captured output and audit is a release gate, not yet done
blocked.ratchet: docs/product/legacy-http-consumers.txt in chip-rs may only shrink

blockers: the agent-parity workflow must pass on main with a freshly built Zig binary and reproduce docs/rebuild/evidence/agent-parity.json (the committed evidence was generated with a prebuilt 0.0.4 binary)
the retirement diff must be reviewed before any Zig agent-loop code is deleted or disabled
blocked.accepted_limitations: Owner decision 2026-10-16: the two crash-recovery differences are accepted as known limitations (conditional on the visible retry warning) and the ten unsupported behaviors are declared unsupported in the first Rust release. See docs/rebuild/parity/agent-loop.v1.json and chip-rs docs/product/release-limitations.md. This is not a claim of parity.

blocked.what: Zig session store and event-log format
blockers: interrupted-turn persistence not ported in the Zig-compatible format end to end (chip-session/chip-turns write the format; cross-implementation CI covers resume only)
Zig remains the only writer for sessions started by Zig surfaces

blocked.what: TUI, ACP, gateway, MCP, SDK (N-API/WASM) surfaces and the tool/builtin layer
blockers: no Rust gateway or MCP client/server (src/gateway, src/core/mcp)
tools and builtins (src/tools, src/builtins) are not ported
SDK N-API/WASM entry points (napi_core_main.zig, wasm_core_main.zig) still build the shipped SDK

single_executor.note: No other crate under rust/ may define an execute entry point or an HTTP client

zig_free_rust.note: Rust code under rust/ may not build, link or load Zig outputs

agent_parity.note: The zig-agent-loop entry may leave `blocked` only when the stored result says retirement_ready: true. The checker validates the stored result against the corpus; it never redefines what must match.
